AcceptReport.description:
What ``engine.proposals.accept`` and ``apply`` did.

``accepted``: the proposals now accepted; ``files_written``: each file
written, once; ``warnings``: such as an earlier knowledge source shadowing
what was written; ``refused``: proposal id to why it was not accepted (or,
from ``apply``, rejected); ``rejected``: the proposals ``apply`` rejected.
AcceptReport.title: AcceptReport

AcceptRequest.description: ``POST /proposals/accept``: ids, and per id the fields to merge over its change before it is written.
AcceptRequest.title: AcceptRequest

AnswerSource.description:
Where an answer came from.

``{"type": "verified", "id", "datasource_id", "params"}`` when a verified
query from ``curated.yaml`` answered, with the values it ran with;
``{"type": "generated"}`` (the other fields None) when the pipeline
planned and generated the SQL.
AnswerSource.title: AnswerSource

ApiKey.description: An API key as `engine.api_keys` lists it: never the secret (D127).
ApiKey.title: ApiKey

ApiKeyCreated.description: The new key and its `token`, shown once: only a hash of it is stored.
ApiKeyCreated.title: ApiKeyCreated

ApiKeyRequest.description: ``POST /api-keys``: the user the key's requests run as, with their roles.
ApiKeyRequest.title: ApiKeyRequest

ApprovalRecord.description: One stored request: ``status`` is ``pending``, ``granted`` or ``denied``; ``id`` is the request's id.
ApprovalRecord.title: ApprovalRecord

ApprovalRequest.description:
What a person is asked to approve: one sub-query's SQL, bound to the asker.

The generated path pins the run's ``decomposition``, the ``sub_query`` the
SQL answers and its validated ``plan``; the verified path pins the
``verified`` query and its values. ``id`` is a SHA-256, in hex, over every
field but ``reason`` and ``approver_roles``, so the engine can tell an
edited request. ``approver_roles`` is for display: the engine checks the
hook's configured roles.
ApprovalRequest.title: ApprovalRequest

BuilderOptions.description: The chips of the builder: everything on it exists and is readable by the caller (D245).
BuilderOptions.title: BuilderOptions

BuilderQuestion.description: A curated query or a saved answer the person may tick.
BuilderQuestion.title: BuilderQuestion

CaseWhen.description:
Represents a single WHEN ... THEN ... clause in a CASE expression.

Attributes:
    condition (Expr): The condition expression to evaluate.
    result (Expr): The result expression if the condition is true.
CaseWhen.title: CaseWhen

ChartPlan.description:
The typed plan behind a chart: a whole run (its decomposition and a plan per sub-query), or a
verified query. Exactly one; shaped on ``PinnedRun`` (A1).
ChartPlan.title: ChartPlan

ChatToolInfo.description: One enabled tool, as ``engine.chat_tools.list()`` reports it.
ChatToolInfo.title: ChatToolInfo

ChoiceRequest.description: ``POST /knowledge/choices``: a clarification pick, filed as a `term` proposal.
ChoiceRequest.title: ChoiceRequest

ClarificationChoice.description: The caller's pick, passed to ``run_query(choice=...)`` (from L2) to run that option's plan.
ClarificationChoice.title: ClarificationChoice

ClarificationOption.description: One reading of the question: ``a`` is the default, each with a validated plan.
ClarificationOption.title: ClarificationOption

ClarificationRequest.description: What ``QueryResult.clarification`` carries when the run ends ``needs_clarification``.
ClarificationRequest.title: ClarificationRequest

ColumnChange.description: A column on both sides whose type, nullability or primary key changed: ``{"type": (old, new)}``.
ColumnChange.title: ColumnChange

ColumnKnowledge.description: What people say about one column. ``values`` maps a code (a string) to its meaning, on ``role: enum`` only.
ColumnKnowledge.title: ColumnKnowledge

DashboardBuildJob.description: The ticked, reworded tiles of the guided builder (``POST /dashboard-builder/proposals`` made the list).
DashboardBuildJob.title: DashboardBuildJob

DashboardJobResult.description: What ``engine.dashboards.generate`` returns, as a model (not the engine's ``DashboardGenerated`` event).
DashboardJobResult.title: DashboardJobResult

DatasourceInfo.description:
One configured datasource, as ``engine.datasources.list()`` and ``get()`` report it.

``status`` is ``ready`` once ``check()`` (or ``datasources.test``)
connected to it, ``failed`` when it did not (``reason`` says why), and
``unchecked`` before either ran. ``connection`` is the configured
connection with every secret masked. A failed datasource has no
``capabilities``: nothing is routed to it. ``sample_questions`` are the
datasource's own, then the glossary ``examples`` a person accepted (not
scoped to a caller: a caller-facing route filters by the datasource).
DatasourceInfo.title: DatasourceInfo

DatasourceKnowledge.description: One datasource's knowledge. Table and column names are resolved against the live snapshot when used.
DatasourceKnowledge.title: DatasourceKnowledge

DatasourceKnowledgeView.description:
One datasource's merged knowledge as the engine uses it, what the caller may see of it.

``origins`` maps an item (``tables.Invoice.description``,
``columns.Invoice.Total.role``) to where it came from, and ``sources`` to
the knowledge source that set it; derived roles are in ``knowledge`` with
origin ``derived``. ``problems`` are the names that do not resolve
against the live snapshot, and joins whose types cannot be compared.
DatasourceKnowledgeView.title: DatasourceKnowledgeView

DecomposerResponse.description:
The question decomposed into semantic sub-queries and how to combine them.

Call this tool with the decomposition itself as the arguments: sub_queries,
combine_groups, post_combine_ops and unmapped_subqueries at the top level.
Do not wrap them in another object or under any other key.

combine_groups.description: How the sub-queries' results combine; a single sub-query is one standalone group.
combine_groups.title: Combine Groups

post_combine_ops.description: Operations on a combined group's result. Empty when one sub-query answers the question.
post_combine_ops.title: Post Combine Ops

sub_queries.description: One semantic sub-query per datasource-level intent of the question.
sub_queries.title: Sub Queries

unmapped_subqueries.description: Intents no resolved datasource can answer.
unmapped_subqueries.title: Unmapped Subqueries

DecomposerResponse.title: DecomposerResponse

DriftReport.description: One datasource's check: its live database against the snapshot its live build was made from.
DriftReport.title: DriftReport

Estimate.description:
The database's estimate of a query, without running it (``EstimatingAdapterProtocol.estimate``).

``rows`` is the rows the database expects to *read*, added up over the
plan's scan operators (a full scan counts its table, not its filtered
output), so a ``LIMIT`` on the result does not hide a billion-row scan.
``cost`` is the planner's own cost units, for display: comparable within
one database only, never with a limit. ``source`` says what was read, for
people. See docs/architecture/wave_b.md, section 9.
Estimate.title: Estimate

EvalReport.description: What ``engine.evals.run`` returns. ``configs`` maps each LLM config's name to its board.
EvalReport.title: EvalReport

EventInfo.description: What ``engine.events.catalog()`` returns per event: its name, description and data's JSON Schema.
EventInfo.title: EventInfo

ExamplesRequest.description: ``POST /proposals/examples``: starter questions to file as `example` proposals.
ExamplesRequest.title: ExamplesRequest

ExplainedStep.description: One sub-query in plain English, rendered from its typed plan; the same plan always gives the same words.
ExplainedStep.title: ExplainedStep

Explanation.description: The run's plan in plain English: one step per sub-query, and how the steps were combined.
Explanation.title: Explanation

Expr.description:
Unified AST for deterministic SQL expressions.

The 'kind' attribute determines which fields must or may be populated.
Strict validation rules are enforced in `model_post_init`.

Attributes:
    kind (Literal): The type of expression (literal, column, func, binary, unary, case).
    value (Optional[Union[str, int, float, bool]]): Value for literal expressions.
    is_null (bool): Whether the literal is a NULL value.
    alias (Optional[str]): Table alias for column expressions.
    column_name (Optional[str]): Name of the column.
    func_name (Optional[str]): Name of the function.
    args (List[Expr]): Arguments for function expressions.
    is_aggregate (bool): Whether the function is an aggregate function.
    distinct (bool): Apply the function to distinct argument values,
        e.g. ``COUNT(DISTINCT x)``. Only valid when ``kind`` is ``func``.
    op (Optional[str]): Operator for binary or unary expressions.
        ``||`` concatenates strings in every dialect.
    left (Optional[Expr]): Left operand for binary expressions.
    right (Optional[Expr]): Right operand for binary expressions.
    expr (Optional[Expr]): Operand for unary expressions.
    whens (List[CaseWhen]): List of WHEN clauses for CASE expressions.
    else_expr (Optional[Expr]): The ELSE expression for CASE expressions.
Expr.title: Expr

ForeignKeyRef.description: A foreign key of ``table``: its ``columns`` refer to ``referred_columns`` of ``referred_table``.
ForeignKeyRef.title: ForeignKeyRef

GroupByItem.description:
Represents an item in the GROUP BY clause.

Attributes:
    expr (Expr): The expression to group by.
GroupByItem.title: GroupByItem

ImpactedQuery.description: A verified query whose SQL reads something the diff dropped or retyped; ``reasons`` say what.
ImpactedQuery.title: ImpactedQuery

ImpactedRule.description: A role's ``allow`` or ``deny`` pattern that matched a dropped table and now matches nothing.
ImpactedRule.title: ImpactedRule

IndexResult.description:
What an index build did. ``failed`` names the datasources that kept their previous index; the reason is in the
server log, where a connection string cannot reach a client.
IndexResult.title: IndexResult

InspectRequest.description: ``POST /index/inspect``: one retrieval run. Anything left out takes the engine's default.
InspectRequest.title: InspectRequest

JoinKnowledge.description: A join the database does not declare. ``from_`` is ``from`` in YAML.
JoinKnowledge.title: JoinKnowledge

JoinSpec.description:
Specification for a table join.

Attributes:
    left_alias (str): Alias of the left table.
    right_alias (str): Alias of the right table.
    join_type (Literal): Type of join (inner, left, right, full).
    condition (Expr): The join condition expression.
JoinSpec.title: JoinSpec

KnowledgeSourceInfo.description: One knowledge source as ``engine.knowledge.sources`` reports it.
KnowledgeSourceInfo.title: KnowledgeSourceInfo

KnowledgeUsed.description: The knowledge one sub-query's prompt carried in ``[BUSINESS_CONTEXT]``, and what the block's cap dropped.
KnowledgeUsed.title: KnowledgeUsed

LLMCallUsage.description: One model call: which node made it, on which model, and what it used (None: not reported).
LLMCallUsage.title: LLMCallUsage

MetricOption.description: A glossary term that names columns the caller can read.
MetricOption.title: MetricOption

ModelChoice.description: One agent's model: the provider and the model name.
ModelChoice.title: ModelChoice

OrderItem.description:
Represents an item in the ORDER BY clause.

Attributes:
    expr (Expr): The expression to order by.
    direction (Literal): The sort direction (asc, desc).
OrderItem.title: OrderItem

PlanModel.description:
Standardized representation of a SQL execution plan.

Every list is ordered by its own position: the first table is the ``FROM``
table, the first select item is the first column, and so on. JSON arrays
keep their order through structured output, so nothing in the plan restates
it.

Attributes:
    query_type (Literal): The type of query (default: READ).
    distinct (bool): Whether to select distinct rows.
    tables (List[TableRef]): List of tables involved in the query.
    joins (List[JoinSpec]): List of join specifications.
    select_items (List[SelectItem]): List of items to select.
    where (Optional[Expr]): The WHERE clause expression.
    group_by (List[GroupByItem]): List of GROUP BY items.
    having (Optional[Expr]): The HAVING clause expression.
    order_by (List[OrderItem]): List of ORDER BY items.
    limit (Optional[int]): The LIMIT count.
    offset (Optional[int]): The OFFSET count.
    reasoning (Optional[str]): Explanatory text for the plan generation.
PlanModel.title: PlanModel

ProfileReport.description: One datasource's profile: the proposals it filed and how far its bounds let it go.
ProfileReport.title: ProfileReport

Proposal.description:
One suggested change to a person's knowledge or curated answers, waiting in the review queue.

``change`` holds the fields it would set, in ``glossary.yaml``'s or
``curated.yaml``'s shape; ``tables`` every ``datasource.schema.table`` it
names, so a caller sees it only when their scope reaches all of them;
``evidence`` counts and checks, never rows. Build one with ``build``,
which computes ``id``.
Proposal.title: Proposal

ProposalsBody.description: The chips of the guided builder: which sources to draw on, and what was ticked.
ProposalsBody.title: ProposalsBody

approval_ids.description: Ids of approvals an approver granted, from an earlier `needs_approval` run.
approval_ids.title: Approval Ids

choice.description: The option picked from an earlier `clarification_request`; asks the same question again.

QueryResult.description:
Represents the result of a query execution.

Carries everything a UI renders: the plan, the validation checks, a capped
row sample, the SQL, per-node timings and the question's LLM token usage.
The full result set still lives in artifact storage, addressable through
``artifact_refs``. ``result_manifest`` lists the run's saved results (its
manifest: node id, columns, row count, truncated), never their rows; read
those by ``trace_id`` with ``engine.results.page`` or ``engine.results.csv``,
as the caller who asked (``user_context``): nobody else can read them.
``trace_path`` is where this run's trace file was written, or None when
``settings.traces.mode`` did not keep one or the trace store is not the
``files`` store (read it with ``engine.traces.get(trace_id)``).
QueryResult.title: QueryResult

QuestionUsage.description:
What one question cost: totals, per-node roll-ups and every call.

``plan_cache_hits`` counts the sub-queries whose plan came from the plan
cache; each one made no planner call, so it adds no tokens here.
QuestionUsage.title: QuestionUsage

ResultManifest.description: Which results a run produced, and who asked it, written as ``manifest.json`` in the run's folder.
ResultManifest.title: ResultManifest

ResultOwner.description: Who asked a run: the only caller its results are readable by.
ResultOwner.title: ResultOwner

ResultPage.description: ``rows[i]`` is row ``offset + i`` of the result, in ``columns`` order.
ResultPage.title: ResultPage

ResultSummary.description: One saved result of a run: what it is, never its rows.
ResultSummary.title: ResultSummary

RowSample.description: A bounded window onto a sub-query's result set.
RowSample.title: RowSample

Rule.description: A business rule in prose (D40), sent when a sub-query reads one of ``tables`` (empty: every sub-query).
Rule.title: Rule

RuleUse.description: A business rule sent with a sub-query.
RuleUse.title: RuleUse

RunStop.description: A run stopped at a limit: which one, its configured ``value``, and what was ``spent`` when it stopped.
RunStop.title: RunStop

RunWarning.description:
Something a run's answer should say, without failing the run (``QueryResult.warnings``).

Not ``Warning``, which is a Python builtin. ``code`` is an ``ErrorCode``
value (``VALUE_NOT_FOUND``, ``JOIN_FAN_OUT``, ``ALL_NULL_COLUMN``,
``JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED``, ``RESULT_TRUNCATED``, ...), ``node`` the node that
found it, ``message`` what the answer says, and ``sub_query_id`` the
sub-query it is about, when it is about one. ``detail`` holds what a
program may branch on; it never holds result rows or sample values.
``detail["recovered"]`` is True for an earlier attempt's error that a
retry has since replaced: the trace of a retry, not something the answer
says.
RunWarning.title: RunWarning

SaveReport.description: What ``engine.answers.save`` did. The answer is always saved (D241); the proposal may not be filed.
SaveReport.title: SaveReport

SavedAnswer.description:
One answer its owner kept: the question and the typed plan that answered it. No rows and no SQL text are
stored; a re-run builds both again under the viewer's scope (D240).
SavedAnswer.title: SavedAnswer

ScheduleIdentity.description: D134: the owner, as they were when they set the schedule. Stored only on the schedule.
ScheduleIdentity.title: ScheduleIdentity

SchemaDiff.description:
What changed in a datasource's structure between ``from_version`` and ``to_version``.

It compares exactly what the schema fingerprint covers: tables, columns,
their types, nullability and primary keys, foreign keys, and the
``engine_type``, which is ``(old, new)`` when it changed. A rename is a
drop and an add. ``to_version`` is None for the live database, which has
no version. A table that was added or dropped is listed once, without its
columns or foreign keys.
SchemaDiff.title: SchemaDiff

SelectItem.description:
Represents an item in the SELECT clause.

Attributes:
    expr (Expr): The expression to select.
    alias (Optional[str]): The alias for the selected expression.
SelectItem.title: SelectItem

dashboard_id.description: Opens the chat on this dashboard (the caller's, draft or saved), so the model can edit it.
dashboard_id.title: Dashboard Id

datasource_id.description: Every question of the conversation skips routing and asks this datasource.
datasource_id.title: Datasource Id

StepRef.description:
An ``ask`` step of the conversation, by turn and step number (both 1-based). Without ``turn``: the latest
turn, which in a chat is the one being answered.
StepRef.title: StepRef

SubQueryResult.description: Represents the result of a sub-query execution.
SubQueryResult.title: SubQueryResult

SuiteInfo.description: One eval suite named in ``evals.suites``: ``path`` is as configured, and ``approved`` counts the cases that run.
SuiteInfo.title: SuiteInfo

TableKnowledge.description: What people say about one table.
TableKnowledge.title: TableKnowledge

Term.description: A business term: what a word means in this datasource, and the columns it is computed from.
Term.title: Term

TermMatch.description: A glossary term sent with a sub-query: what it means, where it came from and how well it matched.
TermMatch.title: TermMatch

TermUse.description: A glossary term sent with a step whose columns the plan reads.
TermUse.title: TermUse

TileProposal.description: One tile to tick, untick or reword. ``ref`` is the verified or saved id; a new question has none.
TileProposal.title: TileProposal

TileRun.description: The last result of a chart; stored with a timestamp.
TileRun.title: TileRun

ToolOutput.description:
What a chat tool returns. Defined here so a stored step can hold one without this module importing
``nl2sql.chat_tools`` (which imports ``Conversation``); tool authors import it from ``nl2sql.chat_tools``.
ToolOutput.title: ToolOutput

args.description: The tool's arguments, as `GET /chat-tools` describes them.
args.title: Args

ToolStep.description: One tool call inside a turn.
ToolStep.title: ToolStep

choice.description: An option id of the pending clarification, sent instead of `text`; the question is asked again with no model call.
choice.title: Choice

execute.description: `false` plans and validates without running SQL.
execute.title: Execute

UsageTotals.description:
Token counts, LLM calls and LLM seconds for one node or one question.

``latency_s`` is time spent waiting on the model, summed over calls; a
node's wall-clock time (which also covers its non-LLM work) is in
``QueryResult.timings``. ``cost`` is null unless every call counted here
has a cost. A token count is the sum of what the calls reported, and
null when no call reported it.
UsageTotals.title: UsageTotals

UserContext.description: Who is asking: the caller's id, tenant and roles.
UserContext.title: UserContext

ValidationCheck.description:
One named validation gate and how it went.

``errors`` records what failed; ``checks`` records what was checked at all,
so a caller can render "structure passed, policy denied" instead of an
empty list meaning success.
ValidationCheck.title: ValidationCheck

VerifiedRef.description: A verified query from ``curated.yaml``, by id, with the values it was bound to.
VerifiedRef.title: VerifiedRef

nl2sql__pipeline__nodes__ast_planner__sc.description:
Represents a reference to a database table.

Attributes:
    name (str): The name of the table.
    schema_name (Optional[str]): The schema of the table.
    database (Optional[str]): The database name.
    alias (str): The alias used for the table in the query.
nl2sql__pipeline__nodes__ast_planner__sc.title: TableRef

get.description:
`engine.about()`: the engine's version, and every step of a run with the model each model step runs on.
Never a key.

schema.title: Response About Api V1 About Get

get.description: The caller's saved answers, optionally those of one datasource.

schema.title: Response List Answers Api V1 Answers Get

post.description:
Keeps the answer of an `ask` step of the caller's conversation and rates its run up. The plan comes from the
stored step, never from the request. The reply says whether a proposal for the shared set was filed
(`proposed`, `proposal_id`) or why not (`not_proposed_reason`). Saving the same run again returns the same
answer.

404.description: No such conversation for this caller.

409.description: The caller is at the cap of saved answers: ANSWER_LIMIT_REACHED.

422.description: The step did not answer, kept no plan, or is not the run named: NOT_SAVABLE.

404.description: No such saved answer (or one that is not the caller's): ANSWER_NOT_FOUND.

get.description: One saved answer, with its question and typed plan.

404.description: No such saved answer (or one that is not the caller's): ANSWER_NOT_FOUND.

post.description:
Runs the stored plan again as the caller: their data scope, hooks and approvals apply, and no model is
called. `approval_ids` are request ids granted through `/approvals`. A plan the schema has outgrown comes back
with status `error` and a first error coded `TILE_NEEDS_FIXING`.

404.description: No such saved answer (or one that is not the caller's): ANSWER_NOT_FOUND.

get.description:
Every key, newest first, revoked ones included: its `id`, `label`, user, tenant, roles, who made it and
when. Never a token or a hash. Admin only.

schema.title: Response List Api Keys Api V1 Api Keys Get

403.description: The caller holds no role in `policies.admin_roles`.

post.description:
A key whose requests run as `user_id` with `roles` (and `tenant_id`). The `token` is in this response only:
keep it, the server stores a hash. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Admin only.

403.description: The caller holds no role in `policies.admin_roles`.

422.description: The user is empty or a role is not one of `policies.roles`.

delete.description: The key stops verifying at once. Revoking a revoked key changes nothing. Admin only.

403.description: The caller holds no role in `policies.admin_roles`.

404.description: No such key.

get.description:
The requests the caller asked, plus those their roles may decide, in `status` (default `pending`). Who granted
one is the engine's record and is not returned.

schema.title: Response List Approvals Api V1 Approvals Get

post.description: Deny the request, with an optional `reason`. A run that names it ends with `APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED`.

403.description: The caller holds none of the roles that may approve this.

404.description: No such approval request for this caller.

post.description: Grant the request. The asker then re-asks the question with `approval_ids: [request_id]`.

403.description: The caller holds none of the roles that may approve this.

404.description: No such approval request for this caller.

get.description:
The enabled chat tools: name, description and the JSON Schema of their arguments. `ask` is the
conversation's own and is not listed.

schema.title: Response List Chat Tools Api V1 Chat Tools Get

get.description: The caller's conversations, newest first: id, title, last update and the number of turns.

schema.title: Response List Conversations Api V1 Conversations Get

404.description: `dashboard_id` is not the caller's dashboard.

422.description: The request does not validate, or the facade refused an argument.

delete.description: Deletes the conversation and its turns; its results stay until their own retention.

404.description: No such conversation for this caller.

409.description: The conversation is already running a turn.

get.description:
The conversation with its stored turns and, when the last turn asked one, the pending clarification. Another
user's conversation is a 404.

404.description: No such conversation for this caller.

get.description:
The answered questions of the conversation written up as Markdown, with no model call. A turn that does not
exist, or a conversation with no answered question, is a 422.

parameters.description: Turn numbers to include; all by default.
parameters.name: turns

schema.description: Turn numbers to include; all by default.
schema.title: Turns

404.description: No such conversation for this caller.

422.description: The request does not validate, or the facade refused an argument.

post.description:
Runs the conversation's last question again as a turn of kind `retry`, with no model call of its own. After a
`needs_approval` turn, send the granted request ids as `approval_ids`.

404.description: No such conversation for this caller, or an id in `approval_ids` is unknown, waiting, denied or expired.

409.description: The conversation is already running a turn.

422.description: The request does not validate, or the facade refused an argument.

post.description:
One chat tool by name, as a turn of kind `tool` with no model call: how a client runs a tool the model offered.
Arguments that do not validate are a 422 and store nothing; a tool that is not enabled is a stored error step.

404.description: No such conversation for this caller.

409.description: The conversation is already running a turn.

422.description: The request does not validate, or the facade refused an argument.

post.description:
One turn: the model's bounded loop of tool calls and a reply, stored. A pipeline outcome is not an error: the
turn's `status` is `answered`, `needs_clarification` (answer it with `choice` in the next turn), `needs_approval`,
`stopped` or `error`. Keys and models in the `X-NL2SQL-*` headers apply to the whole turn when `api.request_llm`
is on.

404.description: No such conversation for this caller.

409.description: The conversation is already running a turn.

422.description: The request does not validate, or the facade refused an argument.

post.description:
As `POST /turns`, as events. A refusal (not the caller's, a bad body, a busy conversation) answers with the
error envelope before the stream begins; once it has, a failure is a last `run.failed` event (its `error_code`, or
`UNKNOWN_ERROR` with a fixed message).

200.description: Server-Sent Events: the run events of each question the model asks, a `conversation.step` after each step, and `conversation.turn` last, whose `data.stored` is the stored `Turn`. A `: keep-alive` comment every 15 seconds. Closing the connection cancels the turn and stores nothing. A failure after the stream has begun is a last `run.failed` event.

404.description: No such conversation for this caller.

409.description: The conversation is already running a turn.

422.description: The request does not validate, or the facade refused an argument.

post.summary: Send a message and follow it

get.description:
The chips of the guided builder for one datasource, as the caller may read it: curated queries, the caller's
saved answers, glossary metrics, dimensions, time columns and five time ranges. No model call, nothing runs.

422.description: The datasource has no index or the caller cannot reach it (NOT_INDEXED), an unknown source or range, or no key for a new question (MISSING_PROVIDER_KEY).

post.description:
The tiles a dashboard could have, to tick, untick and reword. Curated and saved ids become tiles with no model
call; with `asked`, one model call turns the chips and `text` into at most three questions (a key is needed: the
server's, or one sent in headers as for `POST /query`). Read-only: nothing is run or saved.

422.description: The datasource has no index or the caller cannot reach it (NOT_INDEXED), an unknown source or range, or no key for a new question (MISSING_PROVIDER_KEY).

get.description: The caller's dashboards of one `status`, newest first, optionally in one workspace.

schema.title: Response List Dashboards Api V1 Dashboards Get

post.description:
Register a datasource in this process from `config`, shaped like one entry of `datasources` in
`nl2sql.yaml` (`id`, `type`, `connection`, ...). It is not indexed: start the `index` job
(`POST /jobs/index`) next. Admin only.

where. A secret is never written into the YAML: a `${env:VAR}` or other reference is kept as it is, and a

anywhere else it is a 422. A save that fails leaves nothing registered, except when the config is
read-only (`403 NOT_WRITABLE`, Docker's mounted config): the datasource then stays registered until the
server restarts.

A body that does not validate, a typo included, is a 422 listing each problem by its path, never a value.

post.description:
Run a natural-language question through the pipeline.

Returns, per sub-query, the plan, the validation checks, the SQL and a capped row sample, plus the written
answer, errors, timings and token usage. A pipeline failure (a refusal included) comes back with status 200 and
`status: "error"`. `execute: false` plans and validates without running SQL. `choice` answers an earlier
`clarification_request`; `approval_ids` names approvals an approver granted. The caller (user, tenant and roles)
comes from the source `api.auth` names, never from the body; no identity is a 401. Where `api.request_llm` is on,
a request may carry its own provider keys and models in headers.

403.description: The request carries keys or models and `api.request_llm` is off.

post.description:
The same run as `POST /query`, reported as it happens, as Server-Sent Events.

Each SSE `event` is the event's name and its `data` line the whole event as
JSON (`name`, `at`, `trace_id`, `tenant_id`, `data`): `run.started`;
`node.started` (`node`, `sub_query_id`) and `node.finished` (plus `seconds`,
`ok`) per pipeline step; `result.manifest` (`results`) as soon as the results
are saved, so a client can start paging them with the event's `trace_id`;
`answer.delta` (`field`: `summary` or `content`, `text`) as the answer model
writes; `sanity.flagged` and `run.limit_reached`; then exactly one of
`run.finished`, the run's summary whose `data.result` is the `/query`
response, or `run.failed` (`message`, `error_code`) when the run could not
finish. A refusal or a provider error is a `run.finished` with
`status: "error"`, as `/query` returns it. Same body, headers and auth as `/query`; a request the engine refuses
outright (a bad choice, a key it may not take) is the error envelope, before any event. A comment line keeps the
connection open while nothing happens; closing the connection cancels the run before its next step.

200.description: Server-Sent Events, the engine's run events: `run.started`, `node.started`, `node.finished`, `result.manifest`, `answer.delta`, `sanity.flagged`, `run.limit_reached`, then one `run.finished` (its `data.result` is the `/query` response) or `run.failed`.

403.description: The request carries keys or models and `api.request_llm` is off.

get.description:
Whether the engine can answer now, from its own `check()` (kept 10 seconds): every required datasource
and at least one is up, every agent's key resolves (unless `api.request_llm` is on, or every agent is on
`replay`) and the index is `ok` or `stale`. 200 `{"status": "ready"}` or 503 `{"status": "not_ready"}` to
everyone. An admin also gets `problems`: each failing datasource and its stage, each agent whose key does not
resolve and the index status, never a secret. An optional datasource that failed is a problem, not "not ready".

patch.description:
Change only the provider and model of the named agents (`engine.llm.set_models`); every other `llm`
setting (`base_url`, `headers`, `prices`, temperatures) stays. The body maps an agent's name, as `GET /llm`
lists it, to `{provider, model}`, or to null to drop that agent's own model so it runs on `default`. Where an
agent's provider changes, its key and `base_url` are cleared and the provider's standard key variable is
used. A choice the server cannot use is a 422 and changes nothing. Like `PUT`, the change is in memory
and per process, logged and audited. Returns the same change as `PUT`. Admin only.

LLM. The change is logged and audited, and not written to any file: a restart reads `llm.yaml`
again. Returns who changed it (`by`) and each agent whose provider or model changed, old and new.
Admin only.

unknown trace, another caller's, or an id that is not a plain token is a 404.

schema.title: Response Get Trace Api V1 Traces  Trace Id  Get

404.description: No such run or result for this caller.

get.description: The caller's workspaces, oldest first.
